# Purpose

Use the student work to assess load-path reasoning, rigid-body equilibrium, two-force-member modeling, internal shear, internal moment, diagram construction, critical-section identification, and engineering judgment.

# Scope of the Base Problem

The base model assumes a straight and initially horizontal arm, static loading, small deformation, uniform distributed weight, a frictionless pin at A, and an ideal inclined two-force actuator. Joint and gripper dimensions are neglected. The horizontal actuator component creates axial force in the equivalent arm, but the assigned MEEN 305 objective is limited to vertical shear and bending moment. Deflection, detailed actuator sizing, pin and bearing stress, fatigue, stability, servo-drive behavior, dynamic robot motion, and FEA are intentionally excluded.

# Supplemental Assessment Structure

- context interpretation and idealization: 20%;
- whole-arm equilibrium and reactions: 25%;
- piecewise shear and moment derivation: 30%;
- diagram interpretation and critical section: 15%;
- engineering recommendation and limitations: 10%.
